owner_sources.excerpt: The essential promise is not merely that a response can be traced to a prior response. It is that an invocation can be answered in full: What exact world was this agent shown?

findings.title: Exact-context claims exceed what is validated and shown
findings.claim: Context selections can label verbatim bytes as summarized and cite nonexistent derivation blocks, while the cockpit never renders its compiled_prompt_preview and sealed invocation inspection omits exact prompt bytes and attempt-level CLI identity.
findings.failure_mode: A manifest can be internally hash-consistent while asserting false transformation lineage; the operator sees labels and hashes rather than the actual world sent.
findings.consequence: The central promise—knowing exactly what each agent saw—can be confidently but incorrectly believed.
findings.response: Require typed transformation receipts with resolving parents; independently validate every selected and omitted source; expose exact compiled bytes and runtime influence receipts in the cockpit.

findings.title: Subscription-only execution is not enforced by the child environment
findings.claim: The environment filter removes names containing a few secret markers but preserves backend selectors, cloud credentials, and provider base URLs that can route official CLIs through developer-billed surfaces.
findings.failure_mode: A machine configured for Bedrock, Vertex, or a custom provider endpoint can execute a Loom invocation outside the promised consumer subscription without Loom recording the authority change.
findings.consequence: Private prompts may cross an undeclared billing and trust boundary, invalidating the execution contract across providers.
findings.response: Construct an explicit minimal child environment and provider-specific consumer-auth allowlist; reject backend selector and developer-cloud state with permanent mutation tests.

findings.title: Workflow packs are declarations without an enforcing engine
findings.claim: Allowed transitions, triggers, closure rules, role routes, and context-module modes are validated as JSON but are never consumed by a runtime state machine.
findings.failure_mode: The quaternary pack can claim automatic blinded challenge and frozen-query gates while Loom permits unrelated actions and performs none of those transitions automatically.
findings.consequence: The first complete German workflow and any later workflow pack cannot inherit their declared epistemic guarantees from Loom.
findings.response: Compile packs into an executable transition/trigger machine; block undeclared transitions; attach required contexts; generate challenger invocations and authority receipts from canonical state.

findings.title: External workflow writes have no durable idempotency boundary
findings.claim: Workflow command POSTs invoke gatherctl without a lease or idempotency key, then persist only a hash receipt after the external command returns.
findings.failure_mode: A lost response or process failure after the quaternary database mutates can cause a retry to repeat the write; the exact returned object is not preserved as a Loom artifact.
findings.consequence: Canonical quaternary state and Loom history can diverge precisely at the authority boundary the workflow exists to govern.
findings.response: Add generation-bound command intents, leases, stable idempotency keys accepted by the authoritative writer, durable result bytes, and reconciliation for unknown outcomes.

findings.title: The append-only ledger cannot rebuild its derived state
findings.claim: Events omit the full manifests, context provenance, role authority, attempts, and slice bodies required to reconstruct current tables, and no replay/rebuild path exists.
findings.failure_mode: Restart works only because mutable derived tables survive; corruption or a future migration cannot recover the lattice from the claimed append-only truth.
findings.consequence: A broad storage fault invalidates the durable-history guarantee and leaves no independent canonical recovery path.
findings.response: Either make complete versioned events canonical with deterministic rebuild, or explicitly make immutable object tables canonical and narrow the ledger claim; prove fresh-database replay equivalence.

findings.title: Provider artifacts disappear after successful execution
findings.claim: The response schema requires artifacts, but the supervisor reads only payload.response; artifact rows, blocks, edges, and inspector data are never created.
findings.failure_mode: A successful provider can return a cited file or structured proof and Loom silently discards it while marking the attempt succeeded.
findings.consequence: Downstream joins and workflow evidence cannot consume or inspect one of the invocation contract’s promised outputs.
findings.response: Persist each artifact with exact bytes, media type, lineage, produced edges, and inspector exposure before terminal success.

findings.title: Trailheads are roots rather than branch tips
findings.claim: The query excludes invocations that have parent edges, selecting nodes with no parents; the edge orientation is child source to parent target, so leaf trailheads are omitted.
findings.failure_mode: After one follow-up the cockpit offers the initial invocation as the continuation point instead of the live tip.
findings.consequence: Ordinary conversational steering branches from the wrong place unless the user manually finds and checks history.
findings.response: Select invocations that are not the target of any child-to-parent inheritance edge and regression-test forks and joins.

findings.title: Ordinary role creation leaves orphan context on failure
findings.claim: create_role commits the instruction context block in one transaction and inserts the role in a later transaction; a duplicate role name leaves the first write durable.
findings.failure_mode: Validation or uniqueness failures create invisible, unreferenced private blocks and events despite the operation reporting failure.
findings.consequence: Repeated mistakes pollute the canonical lattice and make failed operations observably non-atomic.
findings.response: Move dependent object creation into one transaction with prewritten content-addressed bytes and add failure-stage mutations for bootstrap and draft creation.

findings.title: The clean wheel omits the cockpit and workflow packs
findings.claim: Hatch packages only the loom Python package; a built wheel contains neither web/dist nor workflow_packs/quaternary.
findings.failure_mode: Outside the repository, the service falls back to an API-only page and cannot load the quaternary pack.
findings.consequence: The advertised standalone service is not functionally installable from its own package artifact.
findings.response: Package resources inside the Python distribution, resolve them with importlib.resources, and install-test the wheel in an empty environment.

findings.title: Model-controlled HTML is rendered without sanitization
findings.claim: The cockpit passes marked output directly to Svelte @html without a sanitizer.
findings.failure_mode: A model response can inject same-origin visual controls, misleading forms, links, or layout even where CSP blocks inline script execution.
findings.consequence: Untrusted provider output can impersonate the operator surface and distort consequential routing decisions.
findings.response: Sanitize rendered Markdown with a maintained allowlist library and add malicious HTML/URL mutation fixtures.

findings.title: Gemini and Grok expose private prompts in process arguments
findings.claim: Those adapters place the complete prompt after --prompt or --single rather than sending it through stdin or a protected request file.
findings.failure_mode: Other local processes and diagnostic tooling can observe private project evidence in the command line.
findings.consequence: The future German native lane violates the plan’s explicit prompt-privacy boundary before qualification.
findings.response: Use a documented stdin or protected-file transport; otherwise mark the provider lane unavailable.

residuals.statement: Five S1 and six S2 findings remain active; remediation and independent mutation rejection are required before closure.
The canonical Surface census covers Loom itself; model-runner, Slate, and Axial integration entry paths are explicitly inspected subjects but are not recursively represented in that Surface.
The authoritative German quaternary preparation remains calibrating, so authenticated end-to-end closure cannot yet be claimed.
